# Life comes only from life (spontaneous generation refuted) (`spontaneous_generation_refuted`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/biology.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Life sciences (`biology`)
- Deps: helped by microscope, microorganisms, heat_sterilisation
- Core idea: Maggots, worms, mould and the tiny creatures in broth do not form from rotting matter; each comes from parents or germs of its own kind that got in from outside. Two experiments show it. Put meat in two jars and cover one with fine gauze: flies lay eggs only where they can reach the meat, and only there do maggots appear (Redi). Boil broth in a flask whose neck is drawn out into a long downward S-bend: air passes freely, dust settles in the bend, and the broth stays clear for years; tilt the flask so the broth touches the bend, or break the neck, and it clouds within days (Pasteur). So food, wounds and wine spoil because something living enters them, and can be protected.
- Pitfalls:
  - Boiling too briefly; hay and soil carry spores that survive an hour of boiling, which is why honest opponents kept getting growth
  - Sealing the flask, which invites the reply that the air was spoiled; the open swan neck answers that
  - Claiming to have proved that life can never arise from non-living matter; the experiments show only that it does not happen in broth today
  - Presenting Redi as settling it; he still thought gall insects arose from plants, and microbes reopened the dispute
- History: greece: 4th c. BC – Aristotle teaches that some insects, eels and shellfish arise from mud and decay; the influential view in European natural history for centuries; china: antiquity onward – the same assumption, e.g. insects born from rotting grass or damp; europe: 1668 – Redi's gauze-covered jars; 1748 Needham claims microbes arise in boiled gravy; 1765 Spallanzani refutes him with longer boiling in sealed flasks; 1837 Schwann; 1859–1864 Pasteur against Pouchet, swan-neck flasks; 1877 Tyndall explains remaining failures by heat-resistant spores
- Read:
  - Francesco Redi, Esperienze intorno alla generazione degl'insetti (1668)
  - Louis Pasteur, Mémoire sur les corpuscules organisés qui existent dans l'atmosphère (1861)
  - John Farley, The Spontaneous Generation Controversy from Descartes to Oparin (1977)
